title: Episode 02 — We Followed the Filings
footer: THE SENTINEL REPORT · DOCUMENTS FIRST · CONCLUSIONS LAST
_production: STATUS: SKELETON. Every scene below is one I can stand behind from the
repository itself — how the registers differ, what a filing does and does
not assert, and where this toolkit stops. THE NUMBERS ARE NOT IN IT YET,
and that is deliberate.
WHY THERE ARE NO FIGURES HERE YET
The draft report this was built from carries a FARA corpus of 3,912
records across four registrations, a 536-registrant sweep with 448
UNKNOWN, and a lobbying matrix of 7,130 client-registrant relationships.
THERE IS NO FARA CONNECTOR IN THIS REPOSITORY. `connect test` lists
thirteen: opensanctions, courtlistener, federalregister, fec, senatelda,
regulationsgov, bls, opencorporates, fedregdoc, fedregtext, cldocket,
clparties, usaspending. None of them reads FARA.
So those figures did not come from this desk, and a number whose register
cannot be named is the exact thing this programme exists to refuse. They
may be perfectly correct and from a tool that is not in this repo. Until
that is established they do not go on screen.
THE COMMANDS THAT WOULD PUT FIGURES IN
bin/sentinel connect matrix                 writes the CSVs the LDA
counts come from; read them
back rather than quoting a
terminal line
bin/sentinel connect vendor "NAME" --pages 25
bin/sentinel connect fecpac "COMMITTEE" --cycle 2026
bin/sentinel connect control C00… C00…      shared officers, or NOT
bin/sentinel connect asymmetry --dimension vendor
EVERY FIGURE NEEDS THREE THINGS BEFORE IT IS A SCENE:
1  the register it came from, named on screen
2  a denominator, or the word FLOOR or CEILING beside it
3  a `sdesk claim` with a tier and a citation
THE NUMBER TRAP THIS EPISODE IS ABOUT
A committee's own contributions, money it FORWARDED for earmarking,
independent expenditures FOR, and independent expenditures AGAINST are
four different things. They must never be added. Forwarded money is not
the committee's money at all — it belongs to the individual donors.
BUILD:
python3 ../../engine/shots.py  --spec episode.json
python3 ../../engine/shots.py  --spec episode.json --check
python3 ../../engine/openmontage.py --spec episode.json --check-safe
python3 ../../engine/openmontage.py --spec episode.json --out builds/ep02.mp4

scenes.title: We Followed the Filings
scenes.sub: Lobbying, political money, and the difference between a connection and a conclusion.
scenes.vo: We were not looking for a conspiracy. We were looking for relationships somebody had already put in writing.
scenes.delivery: Flat. You are describing a method, not promising a revelation.

scenes.question: What do the public records actually show?
scenes.delivery: Ask it like you genuinely do not know yet. Because at the start, you did not.

scenes.label: THE FIRST RULE
scenes.quote: A filing is not a finding. It is evidence that something was filed.
scenes.vo: A registration proves a registration. It does not prove wrongdoing, influence, or deception. Everything after this depends on holding that line.
scenes.delivery: Slower than everything around it. This is the thesis.
scenes.source_note: GREEN — this is the standing rule in the repository, not a claim about any organisation.

scenes.label: FOUR REGISTERS, FOUR QUESTIONS
scenes.quote: FARA asks who acts for a foreign principal. The Lobbying Disclosure Act asks who was hired to lobby. The FEC asks where political money went. Corporate registries ask what the entity legally is.
scenes.source: Source: 22 U.S.C. 611 et seq.; 2 U.S.C. 1603-1604; 52 U.S.C. 30104; state corporate registries
scenes.vo: Four databases. Four different questions. Most bad reporting comes from asking one of them a question it was never built to answer.
scenes.delivery: Even pace. Let each one land separately.
scenes.source_note: GREEN — statutory. Cited to the statutes, not to a search result.

scenes.label: WHAT A LOBBYING FILING ASSERTS
scenes.quote: A firm filed a sworn statement that it lobbied for this client, on these issues, before these chambers and agencies.
scenes.source: Source: Senate LDA quarterly filing, form LD-2, 2 U.S.C. 1604
scenes.vo: That is a real assertion, under penalty. It is much stronger than two names turning up in the same search.
scenes.delivery: Confident. This is the strongest thing in the episode.
scenes.source_note: GREEN — an LDA filing is an asserted relationship. `connect senatelda --client NAME`.

scenes.label: AND WHAT IT DOES NOT
scenes.quote: A lobbying filing names a client, a firm, issues and government bodies. It does not name a politician, and it does not say which side the client took.
scenes.source: Source: LD-2 form fields. There is no lobbyist-to-legislator field in the register.
scenes.vo: There is no lobbyist-to-legislator column, because the register has no such field. Any tool that shows you one has inferred it. The politician layer is a different file entirely.
scenes.delivery: This is the correction. Say it like a correction.
scenes.source_note: GREEN — this is printed verbatim by `connect matrix` at the foot of every run.

scenes.question: If one firm represents hundreds of clients, what has it actually told you?
scenes.delivery: This is the honest hard question. Do not answer it too quickly.

scenes.label: SHARED COUNSEL IS NOT SHARED PURPOSE
scenes.quote: A shared lobbying firm establishes a professional relationship. It does not establish a shared objective, a coordinated campaign, or knowledge of one another.
scenes.source: Source: Sentinel editorial standard — the co-occurrence boundary
scenes.vo: A large firm representing a tech company and an energy company and a defence contractor has told you about the firm. It has told you nothing about whether those three ever spoke.
scenes.delivery: Firm. This is the sentence that keeps the episode defensible.
scenes.source_note: GREEN — the standing rule. `connect nexus` grades exactly this as CO-OCCURRENCE.

scenes.label: FOUR NUMBERS THAT ARE NOT ONE NUMBER
scenes.quote: A committee's own contributions. Money it forwarded for donors who earmarked it. Independent expenditures FOR a candidate. Independent expenditures AGAINST one. Four categories. Never a total.
scenes.source: Source: FEC Schedule A, Schedule B, and Form 24 independent expenditure reports
scenes.vo: Forwarded money is not the committee's money. It belongs to the individual donors and passes through. Adding these four together produces a figure that describes nothing that happened.
scenes.delivery: Slow. This is the single most misreported thing in campaign finance.
scenes.source_note: GREEN — `connect fecpac` separates these four and refuses to sum them.

scenes.label: A FLOOR IS NOT A TOTAL
scenes.quote: When a query stops at the page cap, the figure it returns is a FLOOR. The real number is larger by an unknown amount.
scenes.source: Source: FEC API pagination; every Sentinel run that hits the cap says so on screen
scenes.vo: A vendor search that stops at twenty-five hundred rows has not found the total. It has found where it ran out of pages. Those are different sentences and only one of them is true.
scenes.delivery: Matter-of-fact. This is arithmetic hygiene, not drama.
scenes.source_note: GREEN — the page-cap warning is printed by the tool itself.

scenes.label: CONCENTRATION IS MEASURED, NOT ALLEGED
scenes.quote: A vendor paid almost entirely by one committee, and a vendor paid by three hundred, are different analytical objects. Neither is evidence of coordination.
scenes.source: Source: Herfindahl-Hirschman Index over captured Schedule B payments
scenes.vo: Concentration is a fact you can compute. Coordination is a legal question about conduct, and the payment record cannot answer it. The control case is the one that keeps you honest.
scenes.delivery: Analytical. You are explaining a measurement.
scenes.source_note: GREEN — `connect asymmetry --dimension vendor` computes HHI and refuses to characterise it.

scenes.label: UNKNOWN IS NOT ZERO
scenes.quote: A request that was rate-limited did not return no records. It returned no answer. Those must never be written down as the same thing.
scenes.vo: This is the error this desk has made more than any other. A search that could not run, reported as a subject with nothing to find.
scenes.delivery: This one is a confession. Deliver it as one.
scenes.source_note: GREEN — the repository documents this failure mode repeatedly. A 403 from a firewall and a 429 from a rate limit both produce a silence that looks exactly like absence.

scenes.question: Where do you stop?
scenes.delivery: The most important question in the episode. Take your time.

scenes.label: THE CHAIN, AND WHERE IT BREAKS
scenes.quote: Entity. Money. Firm. Other clients. Lobbying issue. Government body. Documented action. Public outcome. We can reach the sixth. The last two are not established.
scenes.source: Source: the evidence map as it currently stands
scenes.vo: We can show you who paid whom, who was hired by whom, and which agency was lobbied. We cannot show you that any of it caused a decision. Nobody has shown us that, and we are not going to imply it.
scenes.delivery: Level. No disappointment in your voice — this is the finding.
scenes.source_note: GREEN — a statement about the boundary of the evidence, which is itself evidence-backed.

scenes.label: WHAT THIS TOOLKIT CANNOT SEE AT ALL
scenes.quote: No connector here reads FARA. None touches labour. None reaches a state officeholder, a county parcel, or a local tax abatement.
scenes.source: Source: `bin/sentinel connect test` — thirteen connectors, named
scenes.vo: Saying which registers we did not search is not a disclaimer. It is the difference between a gap we know about and a gap we would have reported as an absence.
scenes.delivery: Plain. This is a strength, delivered as one.
scenes.source_note: GREEN — verified against the connector registry on 2026-09-15. `connect nexus --gaps` prints the offices that hold the rest.

scenes.title: EVERY DOCUMENT IN THIS EPISODE
scenes.cta: Replace with a real capture sha256 before building. See _production.
scenes.vo: Every record behind this episode is hashed when it is captured, and the hash is in a ledger you can check against the file.
scenes.source_note: PLACEHOLDER — the renderer requires 64 hex characters. Put a real capture hash here: read one from evidence/manifests/provenance.jsonl.

scenes.title: Documents first. Connections second. Conclusions last.
scenes.sub: The record does not tell us what to believe. It tells us what to ask next.
scenes.vo: We follow the data. You decide the story.
scenes.delivery: Land it and stop. Do not add anything.
